i0-context.title: Load baseline context
i0-context.imperative: Load the handed-in goal and context (what you are resolving) and the starting questions, if any. Read the glossary and the topic's relevant code/docs. Record pass when loaded.

q1.title: Wiring scope: does the computed per-season burn-rate calibration get wired into mass_model.race_mass/fuel_at_lap now, or ship as a measured-not-wired calibration report first?
q1.imperative: DEFAULT_BURN_PER_LAP_KG currently feeds race_mass/fuel_at_lap, which are already consumed downstream by layer2 session_braking/session_traction/session_coast/session_estimator, utilization/car_prior (via quali_mass only), and the W3 race_stint tyre-age pipeline (session_race.load_race_stints calls race_mass per clean lap). Wiring a per-season multiplier in now changes those already-closed epics' numeric outputs (#511/#563 tyre-age). Ask the human whether to (a) wire immediately (recompute affected fits), or (b) ship the calibration as a standalone measured module/report first (matches the repo's established 'measured-not-wired' pattern for physics findings, e.g. #512/#511) and defer wiring to a follow-up decision once the correction is validated.

q2.title: Re-batch scope: does wiring the calibration require re-running previously-computed physics/tyre-age batches in this issue?
q2.imperative: Wiring per-season burn rate changes race_mass's output going forward, but existing stored artifacts (data/physics_estimates.db session_estimates, data/race_stint_estimates.db from the closed W3 #511/#563 tyre-age epic) were computed with the flat 1.8 kg/lap and will NOT retroactively update. Ask whether re-running those batch populations is in scope for this issue, or should be filed as a separate follow-up (triage) once the calibration lands, given it is a substantial season-long batch job distinct from writing the calibration itself.

consolidation.summary: Issue 575: per-season fuel burn rate calibration. RESOLVED: (1) wire immediately into mass_model (accept re-validation cost on layer2/W3 tyre-age fits, that recompute is a separate follow-up per (3)); (2) anchor circuits specified as a per-season config map (handles Bahrain absent + Barcelona-Catalunya rename in 2026, not a flat hardcoded list); (3) compute 2026's own calibration factor now from its 7 completed races (Barcelona-Catalunya anchor), shrunk toward the 2019-2025 pooled prior given small sample -- not left prior-only; re-running affected batch populations (physics_estimates, race_stint_estimates) is OUT of scope for this issue, filed as a follow-up triage candidate instead.
